title: Stock Market Today Updates: Sensex surges 1,233 pts, Nifty ends above 23,400; Reliance, Tata Steel top gainers - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Updates - Find here all the updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 2 November 2026

Indian equity markets ended sharply higher on Monday, with the Sensex and Nifty gaining over 1.6 per cent, supported by better-than-expected second-quarter earnings, improving domestic economic indicators and foreign investors turning buyers amid a global rotation in artificial intelligence-related stocks.

The Nifty 50 index closed at 23,440.80, gaining 387.70 points or 1.68 per cent, while the BSE Sensex settled at 75,692.78, rising 1,233.25 points or 1.66 per cent.

Among Nifty 50 stocks, Reliance Industries, Tata Steel, JSW Steel and Shriram Finance were among the top gainers. Infosys, ICICI Bank, HDFC Life, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Axis Bank were among the major laggards.

Also track:Q2 Results Today – Live Updates

In the commodities market, Brent crude oil prices declined more than 4 per cent to USD 108.54 per barrel on Monday. While prices have eased compared with last week, they remain above their long-term average.

Gold prices continued to remain weak, trading at Rs 1,38,420 per 10 grams for 24-karat gold. Silver prices, however, gained 1.65 per cent to Rs 1,82,094 per kg at the time of reporting.

On the currency front, the rupee weakened 21 paise to 94.97 against the US dollar on Monday, compared with Friday’s close of 94.76. It opened at 94.90.

ValueQuest Tristar Fund, a private equity fund focused on India’s advanced manufacturing sector, has secured over ₹2,100 crore in investor commitments within 15 months of its first close, exceeding its original fundraising target, including the full greenshoe.

The Fund focuses on aerospace, defence, precision engineering and energy-transition-linked manufacturing. Its portfolio includes four companies: Hi-Q Electronics, Rangsons Aerospace, Waaree Energy Storage Solutions and Trusted Aerospace & Engineers (TASE Global).

“India is at the beginning of a multi-decade transformation in advanced manufacturing. But sector growth alone does not guarantee investment returns. The real differentiator is identifying the right businesses at the right stage of their evolution. The work we do upfront gives us the conviction to partner with strong promoters and deepen our exposure as they deliver against milestones,” said Aniket Dharamshi, Co-Founder and Managing Partner, ValueQuest Investment Advisors.

“In advanced manufacturing, competitive advantage is built over years through process expertise, rigorous customer qualification and consistent delivery on quality and reliability. Once a supplier becomes integral to a customer’s critical programs, replacing it can involve significant time, cost and execution risk. We seek businesses that can build on these capabilities to deepen customer relationships and translate industry growth into sustained, profitable growth,” said Dr. Arvind Ananthanarayanan, Partner, ValueQuest Private Equity.

ValueQuest Private Equity manages over ₹6,000 crore across two investment strategies, three funds and co-investments.

According to Monarch AIF’s analysis, 130 listed companies that grew their R&D expenditure by over 20% CAGR between FY21 and FY26 delivered average stock returns of 23.5%, compared to 13.7% by the NSE 500 TRI. Interestingly, companies combining strong R&D growth with higher R&D intensity delivered even stronger returns of 32.5%.

Indian equities witnessed a relief-led rally, with the Sensex gaining nearly 900 points and the Nifty holding above 23,200, supported by easing crude prices and strong corporate earnings. Brent crude fell 3.3% to $109.66 per barrel amid hopes of progress in US-Iran diplomatic talks, easing concerns around imported inflation and corporate margins. Reliance Industries surged over 8% following a 33.8% YoY rise in quarterly profit, while Jio Platforms gained over 3% on 13.7% profit growth. Metals, autos and energy stocks outperformed, whereas IT and private banks remained under pressure. FIIs had purchased ₹3,598.54 crore in the previous session. Going forward, sustained foreign inflows, crude stability and earnings breadth will determine whether this recovery develops into a durable trend.

For H1 FY27, total income grew by 41% YoY to ₹378 crore, while EBITDA increased by 47% YoY to ₹152.10 crore.

The strong performance was driven by growth across existing parks, the contribution from its Chennai park, and the Bengaluru resorts, which also delivered their best-ever Q2.

Persistent FII selling has significantly reduced India’s weight in global portfolios, raising questions about the sustainability of this trend. Foreign investors have withdrawn over $40 billion so far this calendar year, including more than $5 billion in October. India’s weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index has declined from around 22% in 2023 to approximately 11.29% now, while a single Taiwanese company, TSMC, accounts for over 15%. FII ownership of Indian equities has also fallen from around 18% or more to just over 15%, a 15-year low.

However, this under-allocation could present a contrarian opportunity. Elevated crude prices, currency volatility, geopolitical uncertainty and the growing attractiveness of global AI investments have weighed on India’s appeal. A normalisation of these factors, supported by resilient domestic growth and corporate earnings, could gradually encourage foreign investors to reconsider their India allocations.

Interestingly, FIIs have continued investing in the primary market despite selling aggressively in the secondary market. In October, they sold over $5 billion in the secondary market but invested around half a billion dollars in IPOs up to October 23. Including the Reliance Jio allocation, this investment could exceed $1 billion. This raises questions about the preference for fixed-price allocations, listing gains or differences in investment horizons.
